cover_text:
Georgetown — Sally Long, a long-time resident of the Central Falls-Milton area, was three years into her stay when she was referred to be an outpatient at the Calvert-Carteret Health Center. The stable flaws revealed in her behavioral notebook during their initial training still echo years later.
Her advanced medical needs allowed Long and her family members to visit several times. When she began to visit with her nurses, they noticed that her strabismus muscles were tight and she fidgeted. Long’s muscle problems made it difficult for her to focus.
Marsha Brancato, Long’s primary care physician at the Calvert-Carteret, cautioned her, “She’s not going to be able to go into practice unless she clears this congenital condition that she has. The strabismus and the nearsightedness are the two major causes of difficulty with posture and balance, because her eyes turn inwards now and she has trouble keeping up with my pupils and breathing.”
COLA has been strong in its mission of empowering patients with conditions like her to develop a positive attitude about their medical care. COLA has been able to assist Long in working and doing what she wants, even by placing a bandage on her hands.
COLA continues to support Long’s physician as she and his team work
